decisions.legacy_behavior: The v1 product contract accepts exactly 0, 30 and 50 percent and rejects every other value.
decisions.graph_behavior: Accepts exactly the same evidenced 0, 30 and 50 percent discounts.
decisions.risk: Reintroducing the former technical 0-through-100 range would create unevidenced product semantics and diverge from the public UI choices.
decisions.recommendation: Keep 0, 30 and 50 percent as the shared v1 product contract.
alternatives: Restrict the product contract to 0, 30 and 50 percent.
Extend the graph contract to all integer values after evidence and tests exist.
decisions.required_product_owner_decision: Accepted for v1: the public SL-discount domain is exactly 0, 30 and 50 percent.
evidence: apps/ge-calculator/ge_calculator_gui.py and apps/web/index.html expose only 0, 30 and 50
tests/test_solver.py and tests/web_solver.test.mjs reject every other value

decisions.legacy_behavior: The v1 input boundary rejects negative progress and progress above the vehicle RP total.
decisions.graph_behavior: Rejects the same invalid progress as invalid_input with structured evidence.
decisions.risk: Permissive clamping would conceal corrupt saved progress and could produce a seemingly valid calculation from invalid input.
decisions.recommendation: Keep strict rejection at every public calculation boundary.
alternatives: Adopt strict rejection for both engines.
Keep clamping but emit a mandatory structured warning.
Retain different contracts and keep the graph path non-productive.
decisions.required_product_owner_decision: Accepted for v1: invalid progress is rejected and never normalized silently.

decisions.legacy_behavior: The v1 input boundary rejects researched=True unless numeric RP equals the vehicle RP total.
decisions.graph_behavior: Rejects the same conflict as invalid_input with INPUT_RESEARCH_FLAG_RP_CONFLICT evidence.
decisions.risk: Choosing either field silently would discard evidence of inconsistent saved progress and could change costs without user intent.
decisions.recommendation: Reject the conflicting state until its source data is corrected.
alternatives: Treat researched=True as authoritative and normalize RP to total.
Treat numeric RP as authoritative and clear researched=True.
Reject the conflict until the user resolves it.
decisions.required_product_owner_decision: Accepted for v1: neither field silently overrides the other; the conflict is invalid input.

decisions.legacy_behavior: Legacy does not expose a structured partial-cost contract.
decisions.graph_behavior: Partial results expose only diagnostic per-line and partial values; owned GE is not applied and no binding totals are emitted.
decisions.risk: Applying owned GE to an incomplete sum would present a deceptively precise remainder.
decisions.recommendation: Keep owned GE unapplied until all prerequisites and totals are complete.
alternatives: Show a separately labelled provisional subtraction without calling it a total.
decisions.required_product_owner_decision: Accepted for Shadow Mode and any future product proposal unless explicitly superseded.
evidence: Accuracy 5 merge clarification: partial results have no binding totals

decisions.legacy_behavior: The production solver selects a deterministic rank-unlock vehicle combination using its existing cost-aware routine.
decisions.graph_behavior: LegacyRankCompatibilityStrategy delegates only Shadow Mode rank selection to that unchanged routine.
decisions.risk: Treating the bridge as graph semantics would silently make the existing Legacy rank-selection policy a permanent Graph contract.
decisions.recommendation: Keep the bridge quarantined and comparison-backed; do not expand optimizer scope before 1.0 and require an explicit decision before any Graph default switch.
alternatives: Specify a separate rank-selection contract only after the 1.0 product goal is complete.
Leave rank-selection cases partial until such an optimizer exists.
decisions.required_product_owner_decision: The comparison-only status is accepted; no optimizer expansion belongs to the pre-1.0 scope.
